t: The Signature Stack: One Compose for the Whole AI Lab
title: The Signature Stack: One Compose for the Whole AI Lab
description: The Signature stack is Justin Addam Higgins' reference compose file — Ollama (LLM), Open WebUI (chat), pgvector (embeddings), Jupyter (experiments), and a file browser, one network, one 'up' command. It is the local AI lab as a single file: the demo in this database generates it customized to your GPU memory. One file, whole lab.

demo.program:
services = ["ollama (LLM, GPU)", "open-webui (chat)", "pgvector (embeddings)",
            "jupyter (experiments)", "filebrowser (files)"]
print("Signature stack (one compose, one network, one up):")
for s in services:
    print(f"  - {s}")
print("Demo in this DB generates it sized to YOUR GPU memory.")

title: Signature GPU Memory Planner
description: The Signature planner sizes the stack to the GPU: it takes your VRAM, subtracts system reserve, and recommends which models fit (7B quantized at 8GB, 70B quantized at 48GB) plus container memory caps. The planner is a demo in this database — enter VRAM, get the stack config. No more guessing whether the model fits.

demo.program:
vram = 24
reserve = 2
usable = vram - reserve
print(f"GPU {vram}GB - {reserve}GB reserve = {usable}GB usable")
print("Planner recommends: models that fit + container caps + batch guidance.")
print("Demo in this DB: VRAM in, stack config out. No guessing fit.")

t: Signature Project Template: compose + env + README
title: Signature Project Template: compose + env + README
description: Every Signature AI project starts from the template: compose.yaml, .env (secrets, never committed), data/ and checkpoints/ volume dirs, and a README with the one-command start. The template is the organization — new projects inherit the discipline instead of inventing it. Cookie-cutter consistency across every experiment.

print("Template: compose.yaml + .env (gitignored) + data/ + checkpoints/ + README.")
print("New project = copy template. Discipline inherited, not invented.")
print("Every experiment, same layout: cookie-cutter consistency.")

title: Signature Checkpoint Discipline
description: The Signature rule: checkpoints write to the versioned volume every N epochs AND on interrupt (trap the signal), with the compose file pinning the training image tag that produced them. A checkpoint is only useful if you know exactly what made it — the discipline records provenance automatically. Resume any run, reproduce any result.

demo.program:
print("Checkpoints: every N epochs + on interrupt, to versioned volume.")
print("Image tag pinned in compose: provenance recorded automatically.")
print("Resume any run, reproduce any result: checkpoints with history.")

title: Signature Experiment Ledger
description: The Signature ledger is a simple convention: each training run gets a directory named by date+git-hash+params, with the compose file copied in. The ledger (a markdown index) lists every run with its result. Months later, 'which run made this model?' has an answer. The ledger is the lab notebook Docker never gave you.

print("Run dir: YYYY-MM-DD_githash_params/ + compose copy inside.")
print("Ledger.md: every run, params, result. 'Which run made this?' -> answered.")

title: Signature vs Ad-Hoc Docker Use
description: Ad-hoc: docker run commands in shell history, latest tags, data in containers, host full of pip packages. Signature: compose files in git, pinned tags, volumes for data, clean host, ledger per project. Same Docker — the Signature adds the organization that turns containers from convenient into reproducible.

title: Signature GPU Sharing: Time-Slicing Discipline
description: One GPU, many experiments: the Signature discipline schedules GPU containers — training at night (cron-started compose), inference by day, and a lock file convention so two trainings never fight for VRAM. title: Signature Model Library Volume
description: The Signature model library is a single named volume shared across projects — download llama3.1 once, every project mounts it read-only. No duplicate 40GB downloads per project. The library has a catalog file (model, size, quantization, date pulled). One library, many projects, zero duplication.

demo.program:
print("Single volume: all models, mounted read-only per project.")
print("Download once (40GB), use everywhere. Catalog file: model/size/quant/date.")
print("One library, many projects, zero duplication.")

title: Signature Health Checks in Compose
description: Signature compose files include healthchecks — the LLM service reports healthy only when the API responds, and dependent services wait on it. No more race conditions where the UI starts before the model loads. The compose file encodes startup ORDER, not just startup. Reliability by declaration.

print("Compose encodes startup ORDER, not just startup.")
print("No more UI-before-model races: reliability by declaration.")

title: Signature Backup Ritual for Volumes
description: The Signature ritual: weekly volume backups to the host (timestamped tarballs), before any major experiment a snapshot, and the backup script lives in the project template. 'docker run --volumes-from' on a cron. Volumes hold the value — the ritual protects the value on a schedule, not on hope.

title: Signature Resource Budget Card
description: Each Signature project has a budget card: GPU VRAM allocation, RAM cap, disk quota, and who gets priority. The compose file enforces it via limits. The card is agreed before the project starts — resource fights get settled on paper, not at 2 AM when the training OOMs the inference server.

t: Signature Security Baseline for AI Stacks
title: Signature Security Baseline for AI Stacks
description: The Signature baseline: no privileged containers, secrets in .env (never in images), non-root users in Dockerfiles, published ports minimal, images from trusted sources with pinned digests. AI stacks pull a lot of third-party images — the baseline keeps convenience from becoming exposure. Security as default config, not afterthought.

demo.program:
print("Baseline: no privileged, secrets in .env, non-root users, minimal ports,")
print("         trusted images, pinned digests.")
print("AI pulls many third-party images: baseline keeps convenience from = exposure.")

t: Signature Onboarding: New Machine in 30 Minutes
title: Signature Onboarding: New Machine in 30 Minutes
description: The Signature onboarding: install Docker Desktop, clone the lab repo, run the GPU planner demo, 'docker compose up' the Signature stack — thirty minutes from bare machine to working AI lab. The onboarding doc is tested on fresh machines quarterly. New hardware stops being a setup project.
